text.title: Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) — Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example illustrating the full procedure for `go-http-handlers` against a representative task, followed by Gin reference code for middleware order, the DI handler struct and request binding.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Gin handler for `POST /orders` that takes a JSON DTO, validates, calls `OrderService.Create`, returns 201 with a typed response. Owner: tl:alex; reviewer: tl:bob; cadence: per-release.

list.item: Each prerequisite supplied per the AGENTS.md table; sources linked.
Existing artefact catalogue checked for duplicates (none found).

section.title: Walkthrough
section.p: The team runs the five-step procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml`, recording one paragraph per step. At step 4 the self-check triggers a fix on the rationale (no input cited); re-check passes. The artefact emits with status='ready-for-owner-review'.

list.item: The decision tree in `content/06-decision-tree.xml` saved one round at step 1 by ruling out a duplicate artefact.
Without the self-check at step 4 the rationale would have shipped without input citations.

example.title: Gin — Recovery, RequestID, Logger, then Auth on the protected group
example.code:
// Gin — correct middleware order r := gin.New() r.Use(middleware.Recovery()) // outermost r.Use(middleware.RequestID()) r.Use(middleware.Logger())
// Protected routes with auth v1 := r.Group("/api/v1") v1.Use(middleware.Auth()) v1.GET("/users", h.ListUsers)
example.note: Recovery outermost, Logger after RequestID, Auth only on the group that needs it (r-middleware-order, r-explicit-middleware-composition).

example.title: Handlers as methods on a DI struct
example.note: Dependencies arrive at construction time; the request context is threaded into the service call; errors go to middleware (r-struct-handler, r-ctx-from-request, r-rfc-7807-on-error).

example.title: DTO with binding tags and ShouldBindJSON
example.note: ShouldBindJSON returns the error without writing a response, so the handler owns the single write (r-dto-with-validation, r-should-bind-not-bind).
